items.title: Delhi High Court denies Vinesh Phogat interim relief to participate in World Wrestling Championships trials
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Thursday declined to grant wrestler Vinesh Phogat interim relief to participate in the selection trials for the 2026 Senior World Wrestling Championships starting on September 14. Justice Swarana Kanta Sharma said that the eligibility criteria prescribed by the Wrestling Federation of India (WFI) for the World Wrestling Championships could not be relaxed exclusively in Phogat’s favour at the interim stage. “The interest of the country in ensuring that its representatives are selected through a fair, uniform and performance- based process is of paramount importance. At this interim stage, therefore, this Court is of the view that the eligibility criteria applicable to all athletes ought not to be relaxed in favour of the petitioner alone, particularly when such relaxation may have consequences for other similarly situated athletes who are not before this Court,” the Court observed. The World Championships will take place in Kazakhstan's Astana from October 24 to November 1. items.title: Mumbai court grants bail to TISS student arrested for slogans supporting Umar Khalid, Sharjeel Imam
items.summary: A Mumbai court has granted bail to Abhirup Ashim Paul, a student of the Tata Institute of Social Sciences (TISS), who was arrested for allegedly raising slogans supporting jailed activists Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam. [Abhirup Paul v. State of Maharashtra & Ors.] Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate Dattatray Shankarrao Khedekar observed that Paul had already undergone custodial interrogation for sufficient period. Pertinently, the Court also said that there was no evidence linking him to any Maoist or any other banned organisation. “Prima facie except suspicion, there is no material to link the activities of the accused with mind set of maoist or against the nation or associating with banned organization against India,” the judge noted. The Court observed that having soft copies of the Maoist books and raising campus slogans in support of jailed activists did not amount to anti-national activity and an inference of being a Moaist cannot be drawn from the same. "Merely because of finding of pdf books (on Maoism), the inference of connection with the mind set of maoist can not be draw," the Court ruled.
